title: The Microgravity Science Glovebox as a Platform for Exploration Research on the International Space Station
summary: Description of the Microgravity Science Glovebox facility (255 L work volume, power, cooling, video, nitrogen supply) and its use for exploration research. Written in 2006, before BASS; no BASS data.

items.quote: Research investigations operating inside the MSG are provided a large 255 liter work volume, 1000 watts of dc power via a versatile supply interface

notes: Abstract via OpenAlex; AIAA full text paywalled. A 2007 version (AIAA 2007-546, NTRS 20070013892) was read for PSI-102 and has no BASS content either.

title: Opposed-flow flame spread: A comparison of microgravity and normal gravity experiments to establish the thermal regime
summary: Not read. Title indicates a comparison of BASS-II microgravity and 1-g opposed-flow spread over thin PMMA to establish the thermal regime.
notes: Elsevier paywall; Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar expose no abstract; no NTRS, PMC or repository copy found. Its BASS-II comparison (2.2 mm/s in microgravity vs 2.0 mm/s downward in 1 g) is reproduced in the BASS-II summary report and already in findings[2] of PSI-25.

title: Simplified model for predicting difference between flammability limits of a thin material in normal gravity and microgravity environments
summary: Not read. Title indicates a simplified model for the difference between 1-g and microgravity flammability limits of a thin material.
notes: Elsevier paywall; Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar expose no abstract; no NTRS, PMC or repository copy found. Likely modelling (possibly compared with BASS fabric data).

title: A Correlation for an Effective Flow Velocity for Capturing the Boundary Layer Effect in Opposed-Flow Flame Spread over Thin Fuels
summary: Computational and scale-modelling work proposing an effective-velocity correlation for the boundary-layer effect in opposed-flow spread over thin fuels. No BASS flight data in the abstract.

items.quote: In this work, computational evidence to establish the importance of the developing boundary layer in the kinetic and microgravity regimes is presented.

notes: Abstract via OpenAlex; full text paywalled.

title: Radiation signature in opposed-flow flame spread
summary: Radiation calculation (RADCAL vs TTNH models) for opposed-flow flame spread, to choose infrared imaging bands for quiescent microgravity experiments. Modelling only.

items.claim: Radiation modelling to plan IR imaging; no flight data.
items.quote: The results confirm the importance of radiative heat transfer in the microgravity regime, where the opposed-flow velocity can be mild or even absent

notes: Abstract via OpenAlex; full text paywalled.

title: OS24-1 The Effect of Boundary Layer on Blow-Off Extinction in Opposed-Flow Flame Spread: Results of Experiments and Simplified Analysis(invited,Scale modeling on solid combustion,OS24 Scale modeling,FLUID AND THERMODYNAMICS)
summary: Not read. Invited JSME ATEM 2015 talk on the boundary-layer effect on blow-off extinction in opposed-flow spread (experiments and simplified analysis).
notes: OpenAlex lists it as open access on J-STAGE, but J-STAGE returned a bot-check HTML page to automated requests; no abstract in Crossref, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar.

title: Role of Gas Radiation in the Mechanism of Opposed-Flow Flame Spread in a Microgravity Environment
summary: Not read. Title indicates gas-radiation effects in microgravity opposed-flow spread (SDSU computation).
notes: No DOI; not found on NTRS, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar.

title: Thickness and Fuel Preheating Effects on Material Flammability in Microgravity from the BASS Experiment
summary: ASGSR 2013 BASS results poster/presentation: 41 samples in 115 burns in the SPICE duct, flows up to 40 cm/s, O2 17-21.5%. Opposed spread over SIBAL fabric peaked at intermediate flow; concurrent spread rose linearly with flow and quenched near 1 cm/s; 2.55 vs 1.21 mm/s at about 10 cm/s; Ultem and Nomex HT90-40 did not burn at 21-22% O2 while Nomex III did; PMSA sphere model comparison.

items.claim: Concurrent vs opposed spread at about 10 cm/s: 2.55 vs 1.21 mm/s.
items.quote: Concurrent and Opposed Spread at ~ 10 cm/s 2.55 mm/s versus 1.21 mm/s

items.claim: Ultem and Nomex HT90-40 did not burn at 21-22% O2 and about 15 cm/s; Nomex III did.
items.quote: Ultem and Nomex HT90-40 samples did not burn on ISS atmosphere 21% to 22% O2 Flow speeds around 15 cm/s Similar to 1-g

items.claim: The paper counts 41 samples and 115 burns; the PSI-26 experimental table has 121 rows (n_tests in the record). The difference is probably non-burn rows (e.g. 'SOOT Cleaning') and reused as-run numbers noted in gaps[8], but the table does not say which rows are burns.

notes: Already cited in the PSI-26 record (findings[9], [14]); it adds nothing new to the findings.

title: A novel apparatus for flame spread study
summary: Not read. Title indicates a new ground apparatus (narrow channel) for flame-spread studies.
notes: Elsevier paywall; Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar expose no abstract; no NTRS, PMC or repository copy found. Ground apparatus, so out of scope by its title.

title: Opposed-Flow Flame Spread in a Narrow Channel Apparatus over Thin PMMA Sheets
summary: 8th USNCM 2013 paper: SDSU Narrow Channel Apparatus tests of opposed-flow spread over thin PMMA in 1 g, compared with drop-tower microgravity; 18 mm and 6 mm gaps were unsuitable. No BASS data.

items.claim: Ground NCA compared with drop tower, not with BASS.
items.quote: Tests completed in the SDSU NCA closely compare to actual microgravity conditions seen in drop tower experiments under otherwise the same conditions.
